title: Statistics and Probability
lines: USAT includes about 3 questions on statistics and probability: mean, median, mode and range; reading a small table of data; and simple probability and counting. The numbers are chosen to be friendly, so if your working becomes messy, check your method.
## Averages and spread
- Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values.
- Median = middle value after sorting. With an even number of values, it is the mean of the two middle ones.
- Mode = most frequent value. A set can have more than one mode.
- Range = largest − smallest.
- Adding the same number to every value raises the mean, median and mode by that number but leaves the range unchanged. Multiplying every value by k multiplies all four by k.
- Combined mean: (n₁ × mean₁ + n₂ × mean₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂). It is not the simple average of the two means unless the groups are the same size.
## Reading a table
- Read the headings and units first. Totals and percentages are the usual questions.
- For a frequency table, mean = Σ(value × frequency) ÷ Σ frequency.
- When a table gives percentages, change to counts only when a number is asked for: 35 % of 240 students is 84.
## Probability
- Probability = number of favourable outcomes ÷ number of equally likely outcomes. It lies between 0 and 1.
- P(not A) = 1 − P(A).
- Two dice give 36 equally likely outcomes. The most likely total is 7 (6 ways).
- Independent events: multiply. The chance of two heads in two tosses is ½ × ½ = ¼.
- Without replacement, the second draw has one item fewer in the bag.
## Counting
- If one choice can be made in m ways and a second in n ways, both can be made in m × n ways.
- Arrangements of n different objects in a row: n! = n × (n − 1) × … × 1. For example, 4! = 24.
- Choosing r from n when order does not matter: nCr = n! ÷ [r!(n − r)!]. 5C2 = 10.
## Worked examples
> The marks of seven students are 12, 15, 9, 18, 15, 11 and 4. Find the mean, median and mode.
> Sum = 84, so the mean is 84 ÷ 7 = 12. Sorted: 4, 9, 11, 12, 15, 15, 18, so the median is 12 and the mode is 15.
> A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red?
> Section A has 20 students averaging 60 marks; section B has 30 students averaging 70. Find the combined mean.
> Two coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
> P(no heads) = ½ × ½ = ¼, so P(at least one head) = 1 − ¼ = ¾.
## Mental-maths habits
- To find a mean quickly, guess a central value and average the differences: for 48, 52, 47, 53, 50, take 50; the differences −2, +2, −3, +3, 0 sum to 0, so the mean is 50.
- Simplify probability fractions as you go by cancelling before you multiply.
! Sort the data before finding the median. The middle of an unsorted list is meaningless.
! 'At least one' is easiest as 1 − P(none).
! In a combined mean, weight each group by its size.
## Quick check
- What is the median of 3, 8, 1, 9, 6, 4? (5)
- What is the probability of a total of 7 with two dice? (1/6)
- In how many ways can 5 people stand in a queue? (120)
